chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
'Do not wear wool and animal hair, except for a reason.'

key_terms.الشَّعْرَ: Hair/fur — animal hair fabric (as distinct from wool), e.g., goat hair
key_terms.الصُّوفَ: Wool — textile derived from sheep or similar animals
key_terms.عِلَّةٍ: Reason/cause/necessity — a valid excuse, ailment, or need that makes an otherwise discouraged act permissible

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about wearing wool and animal hair?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prohibits wearing clothing made from wool or animal hair without a valid reason or necessity. This ruling is set in the context of Islamic jurisprudence on dress and purity; wearing rough animal-based fibers like wool or coarse hair was generally discouraged for ordinary situations, but permitted when there is a valid excuse (illness, necessity, or specific circumstances). The original audience — Shia Muslims during the time of the Imam — would have understood this as a guideline distinguishing normal dress from ascetic or necessity-based exceptions.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘Do not wear the wool and the hair, except for a reason’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Qasim ibn Yahya from his grandfather al-Hassan ibn Rashid from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Do not wear wool or hairs unless because of illness.’”
